newsitem.title: USA: America Online to cut 300 jobs.
newsitem.headline: America Online to cut 300 jobs.

text.p: America Online Inc said that it will cut 300 jobs from its total workforce of 5,900 as part of its recent reorganization move to split the company up into three divisions.

The layoffs will be covered by the company's previously announced $75 million restructuring charge that it will write down in its second fiscal quarter. This reserve will also cover transferring some operations and closing down others.
The cuts are coming from the company's GNN Internet access service, which it is closing and folding into the AOL service, AOL Productions and AOL Publishing in Vero Beach, Fla.
The $75 million restructuring charge will also include some other items which will be determined as the quarter progresses, AOL said.

A spokeswoman for the world's largest online service provider said that the job cuts do not represent a downsizing move at the company, which has seen exploding growth in recent years. "The company will continue to grow," she said, adding that AOL just opened up a new customer service call center in Albuquerque, N.M.
"We are going to add another 1,000 to 1,500 (jobs) between now and June," the spokeswoman said.
She said that many of the new hires will be in the company's technology arena and in advertising sales, as it seeks to expand its revenues beyond subscriber fees.

"Although we were able to transfer many affected employees to new positions, there are some people for whom we were not able to find a suitable position in the new company," said AOL chairman and CEO Steve Case, in a letter to employees.

"The bottom line is that the company has moved forward to implement a number of staffing changes that are necessary to align our workforce with the new organization," Case said, adding that there are many painful aspects of any transition.
